content:
Claude is upgrading its Chrome sidebar into a full Cowork session, so tasks and conversations in the browser can carry over across apps.

Claude can now take browser tasks across all your apps

Anthropic announced the change today. Conversations opened in the sidebar are now saved to Claude's conversation history, where users can pick them up in the Claude desktop, web, and mobile apps.

Skills and connectors already configured for an account work in the browser with no extra setup. Chrome Claude can read the current page, and act using the user's existing browser logins — clicking links, switching pages, typing, and filling in forms.

Anthropic's example: a user asks Claude to gather invoice data from multiple vendor portals and build a spreadsheet, then picks the same session up on desktop to drop in local files, or compare against a previous budget.

The update closes a gap in Claude's browser workflow. Until now, sidebar sessions were separate from conversations in Claude's other apps — chat and context didn't sync.

Anthropic recently introduced an in-app browser for Claude Code, which uses a separate profile. The Chrome extension, by contrast, can act on sites where the user is already logged in.

Anthropic notes that browser agents remain vulnerable to prompt injection attacks.

A separate mechanism reviews high-impact actions when auto-approve is on, and Claude still confirms with the user before things like purchases or sharing personal info.

The company says these guardrails reduce — but don't eliminate — the risk.

Availability

The Cowork sidebar is available to Max and Team customers starting today, with Pro rolling out over the coming weeks. Enterprise admins can enable the feature and limit access to approved domains. Chrome Claude is not yet available on other Chromium browsers or mobile.

The release continues Anthropic's push to make Claude workflows seamless across platforms.

Recent additions have included live iOS app testing in Claude Code for Mac, and new controls in Opus 4.8 for longer-running tasks on more products and devices.
